# Jubilees Chapter 26 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob steals Esau's blessing

---

**26:1** During the forty-third jubilee — the sixth year of the seventh week — Isaac called for his son Esau. "I am getting old," he said, "and my eyesight is failing. I don't know how much time I have left.

**26:2** Take your hunting gear — your quiver and bow — and go out to the open country. Hunt me some game, and cook it the way I like. Bring it to me so I can eat it and give you my blessing before I die."

**26:3** Rebekah was listening as Isaac gave these instructions to Esau. As soon as Esau headed out to hunt, Rebekah moved quickly.

**26:4** She called for her son Jacob. "I just heard your father tell your brother Esau: 'Go hunt game for me and cook it the way I like, so I can eat it and bless you before the LORD before I die.'

**26:5** So listen carefully, son, and do exactly what I say. Go to the flock and bring me two good young goats. I'll cook them the way your father loves.

**26:6** Then you'll bring it to him, he'll eat, and he'll bless you before he dies."

**26:7** Jacob hesitated. "Mother, Esau is covered in hair and I have smooth skin.

**26:8** If Father feels my hands, he'll know I'm deceiving him, and instead of a blessing, I'll get a curse."

**26:9** "Any curse that comes will fall on me," his mother said. "Just do what I tell you."

**26:10** Jacob obeyed his mother. He brought back the two young goats, and Rebekah prepared the savory dish exactly as Isaac liked it.

**26:11** Then she took Esau's finest clothes — the ones she kept in the house — and dressed Jacob in them.

**26:12** She wrapped the goatskins around his hands and covered the smooth part of his neck.

**26:13** She handed Jacob the food and bread she had prepared, and he carried them in to his father.

**26:14** "Father," he said. "Yes? Who is it?" Isaac called back.

**26:15** "It's Esau, your firstborn," Jacob said. "I've done what you asked. Sit up and eat the game I caught, so you can bless me."

**26:16** "You found it remarkably fast," Isaac said. "How?" — "The LORD your God helped me," Jacob replied.

**26:17** "Come closer," Isaac said. "I need to feel you — are you really my son Esau?"

**26:18** Jacob came close and Isaac ran his hands over him. "The voice sounds like Jacob," he murmured, "but the hands — the hands are Esau's." He still could not tell, because the goatskins made Jacob's hands feel hairy just like Esau's.

**26:19** He blessed him, then asked once more: "You're truly Esau?" "I am," said Jacob.

**26:20** "Bring the food closer then," Isaac said. Jacob brought it, and his father ate. He brought wine too, and his father drank.

**26:21** "Come and kiss me, son," Isaac said. Jacob leaned in and kissed him. Isaac breathed in the scent of the clothes.

**26:22** And he blessed him: "The smell of my son is like the smell of a fertile field that the LORD himself has blessed. May God give you the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth — grain in abundance, new wine flowing freely.

**26:23** May nations serve you. May peoples bow at your feet. Rule over your brothers; let your mother's sons come and bow before you. Anyone who curses you will be cursed. Anyone who blesses you will be blessed."

**26:24** The moment Isaac finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had barely slipped out the door, Esau came back in from his hunt.

**26:25** He cooked the game, brought it to his father, and said, "Sit up and eat, Father — eat what I caught for you, and bless me."

**26:26** "Who are you?" Isaac asked. "Your firstborn son, Esau," came the reply.

**26:27** Isaac was seized with violent trembling. "Then who was it," he gasped, "who just brought me game? I ate it all before you came — and I blessed him. He will remain blessed."

**26:28** Esau let out a cry — loud, anguished, raw. "Bless me too, Father! Bless me too!"

**26:29** "Your brother came and tricked me," Isaac said. "He took your blessing."

**26:30** "Jacob — of course," Esau said bitterly. "That name suits him perfectly. He's cheated me twice over: first my birthright, now my blessing. Is there anything left for me?"

**26:31** "I've already made him your master," Isaac said. "I've given him your brothers as his servants. I've provided for him with grain and wine. What is there left that I can give you?"

**26:32** "Do you have only one blessing?" Esau cried. "Bless me too, Father — please!" And he broke down weeping.

**26:33** Isaac finally spoke: "You will live far from the rich soil of the earth, with no dew falling on you from above.

**26:34** You'll live by your sword and be subject to your brother. But the day will come when you throw off his yoke and live free."

---

*PNEUMA notes: This chapter parallels Genesis 27 but Jubilees dates it precisely to jubilee 43. The dynamic rendering preserves the drama of the deception while capturing Rebekah's urgency, Isaac's growing suspicion, and Esau's anguish. The blessing and counter-blessing texts follow the Ge'ez expansion faithfully.*
